fund.shortSummary: Small awards for community-led projects that improve reliable access to fresh food in underserved neighborhoods.
audience: Community coalitions with a fiscal sponsor

goodFit: Applicant is a nonprofit or public school
Project serves a documented low-access neighborhood
Request is no more than 25000 USD
poorFit: Applicant is an individual or for-profit business
Project is outside the service region

evaluationGuidance.reviewPriorities: Start with the hard-disqualifier checks: eligible applicant, in-region low-access food focus, request at or below the cap, and non-commercial project type. Treat the pantry partner and match rules as strengthening signals only after hard criteria are satisfied.
evaluationGuidance.borderlineHandling: A request even slightly above 25000 USD misses the cap unless the applicant can reduce this fund's ask. A citywide project can meet the service-area rule only when the answer states a clear low-access focus; do not treat general citywide benefit as enough.
evaluationGuidance.definitions: Use low-access neighborhood to mean the community served, not the applicant's mailing address. Non-commercial food access includes free distribution, pantry logistics, or community growing; standard retail sales alone remain outside scope.
evaluationGuidance.communicationEmphasis: Use practical community-development language. When a gap appears coachable, point to the specific remediation, such as adding a fiscal sponsor, documenting site access, or naming a supplier, without softening hard-disqualifier criteria.

progress.displayHint: Show answered questions over answered plus shortest remaining reachable questions from the current node.

questions.prompt: What type of applicant are you applying as?
questions.helpText: Choose the legal entity or sponsor that would receive the grant agreement.

options.label: Nonprofit organization
options.helpText: Choose this if a 501(c)(3) or equivalent nonprofit would hold and sign the grant agreement.

options.label: Public school or school district
options.helpText: Choose this if a K–12 public school or school district would sign the agreement on behalf of the project.

options.label: For-profit business
options.helpText: A business that generates revenue from commercial operations rather than charitable mission.

options.label: Individual resident
options.helpText: A private resident acting without a sponsoring organization or formal legal entity.

questions.prompt: Where will the project primarily serve people?
questions.helpText: Use the neighborhood where most benefits will occur, not the applicant office address.

options.label: A documented low-access neighborhood
options.helpText: A neighborhood with limited nearby grocery or fresh food options, ideally documented by a food access study or USDA food desert designation.

options.label: Citywide, with a clear low-access focus
options.helpText: The project covers the whole city but deliberately targets and benefits residents in documented low-access areas.

options.label: Outside the eligible service region
options.helpText: The project's primary beneficiaries are in a county or metro area outside the fund's eligible geographic boundary.

questions.prompt: How much funding are you requesting?
questions.helpText: Enter the requested grant amount in US dollars. This microgrant caps awards at 25000 USD.

questions.prompt: Which project type best describes your request?
questions.helpText: Pantry, garden, and retail-adjacent projects ask different follow-up questions because their eligibility evidence differs.

options.label: Mobile pantry or fresh food distribution
options.helpText: Distributes free or low-cost food directly to community members, often by vehicle or pop-up site.

options.label: Community garden or growing site
options.helpText: A shared growing space that produces food for community use, donation, or low-cost sale.

options.label: Commercial retail expansion
options.helpText: A store or market that sells food to paying customers at standard market prices.

questions.prompt: Do you have a named food supplier or distribution partner?
questions.helpText: A letter of intent is enough for the proposal stage.

questions.prompt: What is the status of land or site access for the garden?
questions.helpText: The site can be owned, leased, or covered by a written use agreement.

options.label: Secured
options.helpText: The organization owns, leases, or holds a signed written use agreement for the garden site.

options.label: Pending written approval
options.helpText: A lease or written permission is in active negotiation but has not been signed yet.

options.label: No site identified
options.helpText: No site has been selected or contacted; the location is still to be determined.

questions.prompt: If retail activity is involved, how will food access benefits be provided?
questions.helpText: Commercial expansion is generally outside scope, but record whether there is a non-commercial community benefit for the agent to evaluate.

options.label: Free or no-cost distribution component
options.helpText: A dedicated no-cost component such as a pantry shelf, community fridge, or free bag program alongside any retail activity.

options.label: Discounted fresh produce for eligible residents
options.helpText: A sliding-scale or income-based discount program for fresh produce that reduces the cost for low-income households.

options.label: Standard retail sales only
options.helpText: The project operates as a standard-priced retail store with no dedicated free or reduced-cost food component.

questions.prompt: How much confirmed matching support do you have?
questions.helpText: Include cash and documented in-kind support. Enter 0 if none is confirmed yet.

questions.prompt: When could the project begin after award notice?
questions.helpText: Choose the earliest realistic start window after grant approval.

terminals.title: Confirm your food resilience answers
terminals.message: Review the complete answer summary. After confirmation, the agent will assess eligibility against the food resilience rules and explain any gaps.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The applicant must be a nonprofit organization or public school that can sign the grant agreement for the project.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Apply through a nonprofit organization or public school that can sign the grant agreement, or obtain one as a fiscal sponsor before applying.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The project must primarily serve people in the eligible region and include a documented low-access food focus.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Revise the project so the primary beneficiaries are in the eligible region and document the low-access neighborhood served.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The requested grant amount must be no more than 25000 USD.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Reduce the grant request to 25000 USD or less, or split costs so only eligible expenses are requested from this fund.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The project must be a non-commercial food access project, such as a mobile pantry, fresh food distribution effort, or community garden.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Reframe the project around non-commercial food access, such as free or low-cost distribution, pantry logistics, or a community growing site.

eligibilityRules.criterion: For community garden projects, the applicant must have secured or pending written access to the garden site.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Identify a garden site and obtain ownership documentation, a lease, or written permission from the site owner before applying.

eligibilityRules.criterion: For mobile pantry or fresh food distribution projects, the applicant should have a named supplier or distribution partner.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Secure a named food supplier, pantry network, school, or distribution partner and include their letter of intent to strengthen the application.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The application should document at least 2500 USD in confirmed cash or in-kind matching support.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Document additional cash or in-kind support. For a 25000 USD request, target at least 2500 USD in confirmed match; scale proportionally for smaller requests.
